column1: # Corpus records the x86-64 JIT is known to fail, one per line as
# <record name><TAB><class>. Each class is a correctness gap of the engine,
# not of the record; the JIT corpus test fails when a listed record passes,
# so a fix removes its rows in the same change.
# sse-nan-rules (5): SSE, FMA and SQRT results follow arm64 NaN rules: the
# default NaN is positive and the propagated NaN is not the first source's.
# sse-denormal-rules (4): DAZ and FTZ follow arm64 FPCR.FZ: inputs and min/max
# results flush where x86 keeps them, and tininess is detected before
# sse-estimates (3): RCPSS and RSQRTSS special inputs: the arm64 estimates
# return a denormal or finite value where x86 returns zero or infinity.
